ei.subject: 2026년 3월 고2 모의고사
ei.title: Oliver's First Day at the New School

fullPassage: Looking around the noisy cafeteria, Oliver gripped his tray tightly. He felt the heavy weight of being new to the school. Not knowing how the day would go made him feel anxious. He sat with a heavy sigh at a corner table. He thought, 'Can I make it through the rest of the day?' Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him. It was a boy from his math class. "Hey, is this seat taken? By the way, thanks for lending me that pen earlier." The invisible wall around Oliver seemed to melt away. "Not at all, please sit," he replied. Starting to feel at ease, he smiled brightly at the boy.

questions.passage: Looking around the (A)[noisy / silent] cafeteria, Oliver (B)[gripped / released] his tray tightly. He felt the heavy weight of being (C)[new / familiar] to the school. Not knowing how the day would go made him feel anxious. He sat with a heavy sigh at a corner table. He thought, 'Can I make it through the rest of the day?' Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 시끄러운(noisy) 카페테리아를 둘러보며, Oliver는 쟁반을 꽉 잡았다(gripped). 학교에 새로(new) 온 무거움을 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① noisy — gripped — new: 원문과 일치
❌ ② silent(조용한): noisy의 반의어
❌ ③ released(놓았다): gripped의 반의어
❌ ④ familiar(익숙한): new의 반의어
det.tip: noisy = 시끄러운, grip = 꽉 잡다, new to = ~에 새로 온

questions.passage: Looking around the noisy cafeteria, Oliver gripped his tray tightly. He felt the heavy weight of being new to the school. Not knowing how the day would go made him feel (A)[anxious / confident]. He sat with a heavy (B)[sigh / laugh] at a (C)[corner / center] table. He thought, 'Can I make it through the rest of the day?' Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 하루가 어떻게 흘러갈지 모른다는 것이 그를 불안하게(anxious) 만들었다. 그는 무거운 한숨(sigh)과 함께 구석(corner) 테이블에 앉았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② anxious — sigh — corner: 원문과 일치
❌ ① confident(자신 있는): anxious의 반의어
❌ ③ laugh(웃음): sigh와 정반대 어감
❌ ④ center(중앙): corner의 반의어
det.tip: anxious = 불안한, sigh = 한숨, corner = 구석

questions.passage: Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him. It was a boy from his math class. "Hey, is this seat taken? By the way, thanks for lending me that pen earlier." The (A)[invisible / visible] wall around Oliver seemed to (B)[melt / build] away. "Not at all, please sit," he replied. Starting to feel at (C)[ease / risk], he smiled brightly at the boy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: Oliver 주변의 보이지 않는(invisible) 벽이 녹아(melt) 사라지는 듯했다. 편안함(ease)을 느끼기 시작하며 그는 환하게 웃었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ invisible — melt — ease: 원문과 일치
❌ ① visible(보이는): invisible의 반의어
❌ ② build(쌓다): melt와 반대 어감
❌ ④ risk(위험): ease와 반대 어감
det.tip: invisible = 보이지 않는, melt away = 사라지다, at ease = 편안한

questions.passage: Looking around the noisy cafeteria, Oliver gripped his tray ①<u>tightly</u>. He felt the heavy ②<u>weight</u> of being new to the school. Not knowing how the day would go made him feel ③<u>confident</u>. He sat with a heavy ④<u>sigh</u> at a corner table.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ confident(자신 있는) → anxious(불안한): 새 학교에서 어떻게 될지 모른다는 상황은 자신감이 아니라 불안을 유발한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① tightly(꽉): 쟁반을 꽉 잡음 — 적절
✅ ② weight(무게): 부담감의 무거움
❌ ③ confident(자신 있는): 원문은 anxious(불안한)
✅ ④ sigh(한숨): 무거운 한숨
det.tip: anxious(불안한) ↔ confident(자신 있는)

questions.passage: Just then, a plastic tray was placed down ①<u>opposite</u> him. It was a boy from his math class. The ②<u>visible</u> wall around Oliver seemed to ③<u>melt</u> away. Starting to feel at ④<u>ease</u>, he smiled brightly at the boy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② visible(보이는) → invisible(보이지 않는): Oliver를 둘러싼 심리적 장벽은 '보이지 않는' 벽이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① opposite(맞은편의): 적절
❌ ② visible(보이는): 원문은 invisible(보이지 않는)
✅ ③ melt(녹다): 벽이 사라짐
✅ ④ ease(편안함): 점차 편안해짐
det.tip: invisible(보이지 않는) ↔ visible(보이는)

questions.passage: Looking around the noisy cafeteria, Oliver __________ his tray tightly. He felt the heavy weight of being new to the school. Not knowing how the day would go made him feel uneasy. He sat with a heavy sigh at a corner table. He thought, 'Can I make it through the rest of the day?' Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 긴장한 Oliver는 쟁반을 꽉 잡았다(gripped).
det.analysis:
✅ ② gripped(꽉 잡았다): 긴장의 신체 신호
❌ ① dropped(떨어뜨렸다): 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ threw(던졌다): 무관
❌ ④ ignored(무시했다): 무관
det.tip: grip = 꽉 잡다 — 긴장 상태의 표현

questions.passage: Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him. It was a boy from his math class. "Hey, is this seat taken? By the way, thanks for lending me that pen earlier." The __________ wall around Oliver seemed to melt away.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Oliver를 둘러싼 심리적 거리감은 보이지 않는(invisible) 벽으로 표현된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ invisible(보이지 않는): 심리적 장벽
❌ ① colorful(화려한): 문맥과 무관
❌ ② thick(두꺼운): 물리적 표현
❌ ④ broken(깨진): 의미 모순
det.tip: invisible wall = 보이지 않는 벽 — 심리적 장벽 비유

questions.passage: Looking around the noisy cafeteria, Oliver gripped his tray tightly. He felt the heavy weight of being new to the school. Not knowing how the day would go made him feel __________. He sat with a heavy sigh at a corner table. He thought, 'Can I make it through the rest of the day?' Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새 학교 첫날의 막막함은 그를 불안하게(anxious) 만든다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ anxious(불안한): 새 학교 첫날의 막막함
❌ ① delighted(기쁜): 반대
❌ ② bored(지루한): 무관
❌ ③ proud(자랑스러운): 무관
det.tip: anxious = 불안한, 걱정스러운

questions.passage: Not knowing how the day would go made him feel <u>anxious</u>. He sat with a heavy sigh at a corner table.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 anxious의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: anxious = 불안한, nervous = 긴장한 → 동의어
det.analysis:
✅ ① nervous(긴장한): anxious의 동의어
❌ ② calm(차분한): 반의어
❌ ③ delighted(기뻐하는): 반대 의미
❌ ④ confident(자신 있는): 반의어
det.tip: anxious = nervous = worried = uneasy = 불안한

questions.passage: Looking around the noisy cafeteria, Oliver <u>gripped</u> his tray tightly. He felt the heavy weight of being new to the school.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 gripped의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: gripped = 꽉 잡았다, held tightly = 꽉 잡았다 → 동의어
det.analysis:
✅ ② held tightly(꽉 잡았다): gripped의 동의어
❌ ① dropped(떨어뜨렸다): 반대 의미
❌ ③ pushed away(밀어냈다): 반대 의미
❌ ④ ignored(무시했다): 무관
det.tip: grip = grasp = clutch = hold tightly = 꽉 잡다

questions.passage: The invisible wall around Oliver seemed to <u>melt</u> away. "Not at all, please sit," he replied.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 melt의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: melt away = 사라지다, disappear = 사라지다 → 동의어
det.analysis:
✅ ③ disappear(사라지다): melt away의 동의어
❌ ① harden(굳다): 반대 의미
❌ ② grow(자라다): 반대 의미
❌ ④ remain(남다): 반의어
det.tip: melt away = disappear = vanish = fade = 사라지다

questions.passage: Looking around the <u>noisy</u> cafeteria, Oliver gripped his tray tightly. He felt the heavy weight of being new to the school. Not knowing how the day would go made him feel anxious. He sat with a heavy sigh at a corner table.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 noisy의 의미와 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: noisy = 시끄러운 ↔ quiet = 조용한
det.analysis:
❌ ④ quiet(조용한): noisy의 반의어 → 가장 먼 의미
✅ ① loud(시끄러운): 동의어
✅ ② noisy(시끄러운): 동일
✅ ③ deafening(귀가 먹먹할 정도의): 유사어
det.tip: noisy(시끄러운) ↔ quiet = silent = 조용한

questions.passage: Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him. It was a boy from his math class. "Hey, is this seat taken? By the way, thanks for lending me that pen earlier." The <u>invisible</u> wall around Oliver seemed to melt away. "Not at all, please sit," he replied.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 invisible의 의미와 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: invisible = 보이지 않는 ↔ visible = 보이는
det.analysis:
❌ ① visible(보이는): invisible의 반의어 → 가장 먼 의미
✅ ② unseen(보이지 않는): 동의어
✅ ③ hidden(숨겨진): 유사어
✅ ④ imperceptible(감지할 수 없는): 유사어
det.tip: invisible(보이지 않는) ↔ visible(보이는)

questions.passage: Not knowing how the day would go made him feel anxious. He sat with a heavy sigh at a corner table. He thought, 'Can I <u>make</u> it through the rest of the day?' Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him. It was a boy from his math class.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 make it이 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: make it through = 견뎌내다, 버텨내다. make는 다의어.
det.analysis:
✅ ② manage to survive(잘 버텨내다): 어려운 상황을 견뎌내다
❌ ① create something(무언가를 만들다): 다른 의미
❌ ③ become famous(유명해지다): 다른 의미
❌ ④ earn money(돈을 벌다): 다른 의미
det.tip: make it through = ~을 견뎌내다, 버텨내다

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a long, deep breath that shows you are sad, tired, or relieved"

det.korean: "슬픔, 피곤함, 안도감을 나타내는 길고 깊은 숨" = sigh(한숨)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ sigh(한숨): 감정을 나타내는 깊은 숨
❌ ① yawn(하품): 졸릴 때 입을 벌림
❌ ② laugh(웃음): 즐거움 표현
❌ ④ whisper(속삭임): 작은 목소리
det.tip: sigh = 한숨 | with a sigh = 한숨을 쉬며

questions.passage: Not knowing how the day would go made him feel __________(anxiety).
questions.stem:
다음 문장의 부분을 문맥에 맞게 어형 변환하시오. (1단어)

"Not knowing how the day would go made him feel __________(anxiety)."

det.korean: anxiety(불안, 명사) → anxious(불안한, 형용사): feel + 형용사 구조이므로 형용사형이 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ anxious(불안한, 형용사): feel 뒤에는 형용사
det.tip: anxiety(명사) → anxious(형용사) → anxiously(부사). feel + 형용사

questions.passage: Starting to feel at ease, he smiled __________(bright) at the boy.
questions.stem:
다음 문장의 부분을 문맥에 맞게 어형 변환하시오. (1단어)

"Starting to feel at ease, he smiled __________(bright) at the boy."

det.korean: bright(밝은, 형용사) → brightly(밝게, 부사): 동사 smiled를 수식하는 부사가 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ brightly(밝게, 부사): 동사 smiled 수식
det.tip: bright(형용사) → brightly(부사). 동사 수식 시 부사 사용

questions.passage: Just then, a plastic tray was placed down opposite him. It was a boy from his math class. "Hey, is this seat taken?"
questions.stem: "이 자리 비어 있나요?"를 영어로 옮길 때 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Is this seat taken? = 이 자리 (누가) 잡았나요? → 비어 있나요? (관용 표현)
det.analysis:
✅ ② Is this seat taken?: 영어 관용 표현
❌ ① Is this seat empty?: 어색
❌ ③ Does this seat have someone?: 비문법
❌ ④ Will this seat be free?: 미래시제 부적절
det.tip: Is this seat taken? = 이 자리 비어 있나요? (관용)

questions.passage: The invisible wall around Oliver seemed to melt away. "Not at all, please sit," he replied.
questions.stem:
"Oliver 주변의 보이지 않는 벽이 녹아 사라지는 듯했다."를 영어로 옮길 때 빈칸에 가장 적절한 것은?

The invisible wall around Oliver seemed to __________.

det.korean: 녹아 사라지다 = melt away
det.analysis:
✅ ④ melt away(녹아 사라지다): 원문 일치
❌ ① build up(쌓이다): 반대 의미
❌ ② stand still(가만히 서 있다): 무관
❌ ③ break down(고장나다): 다른 의미
det.tip: melt away = 녹아 사라지다 — 비유적으로 '천천히 사라지다'

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

"feeling relaxed and comfortable, not nervous"

det.korean: "긴장하지 않고 편안한 상태" = at ease(편안한)
det.analysis:
✅ ① at ease(편안한): 긴장 풀린 상태
❌ ② on edge(초조한): 반대 의미
❌ ③ in trouble(곤경에 처한): 무관
❌ ④ out of breath(숨이 찬): 무관
det.tip: at ease = 편안한 ↔ on edge = 초조한
